verdict: Amphenol's sales jumped 65% to $10.2B as the acquired CommScope connectivity business and AI data-center demand kicked in, and net income rose 64% to $2.1B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Vs $0.49 a year ago (two share classes combined)

kpis.label: Communications sales
kpis.note: CommScope deal plus AI data-center demand

segments.name: Communications Solutions
segments.note: Connectors and cable for data centers and networks — nearly doubled, driven by the acquired CommScope broadband/connectivity business and AI data-center demand.

segments.name: Harsh Environment Solutions
segments.note: Rugged connectors for defense, aerospace and heavy industry.

segments.name: Interconnect and Sensor Systems
segments.note: Sensors and interconnects for cars, aircraft and industry.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the now much larger connector group after a year of acquisitions.

opex.name: Acquisition-related expenses
opex.note: Costs tied to the CommScope connectivity business and other deals.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $212M — debt rose to fund the CommScope deal — partly offset by $21M of other income.

takeaways.title: Sales hit $10.2B
takeaways.text: Growth of 65% in dollars mixes the CommScope acquisition with strong organic demand, especially from AI data centers.

takeaways.title: Margins held at scale
takeaways.text: Operating income of $3.02B was 29.5% of sales — a high margin for a manufacturing business, even while integrating a large acquisition.

takeaways.title: Net income rose 64%
takeaways.text: Profit rose from $1.26B a year ago to $2.05B, even with interest expense nearly tripling to $212M on acquisition debt.

footerNote: Consolidated net income is shown; net income attributable to Amphenol shareholders was $2,034M, with $20M attributable to noncontrolling interests.
